# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 39 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 39 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_039_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Part 1 — On the Two Angels

**39:1** "In the first commandment," he said, "I charged you to keep faith, fear, and self-control." "Yes, lord," I replied. "But now," he said, "I wish to make known to you the powers of these commandments, so that you may understand what power each one possesses and what effects it produces."

**39:2** "Two angels attend upon every person," he said — "one of righteousness and one of wickedness." "How then, lord," I asked, "shall I recognize their operations, since both of them dwell with me?"

**39:3** "Hear and understand them," he said. "The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle, and tranquil. When he arises in your heart, immediately he speaks with you of righteousness, purity, holiness, self-control, and every righteous deed and every glorious virtue. When all these things arise in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. Such are the works of the angel of righteousness. Trust him therefore and his works."

**39:4** "Now observe the works of the angel of wickedness as well. First, he is quick-tempered and bitter and senseless, and his works are evil, overturning the servants of God. When therefore he arises in your heart, know him by his works."

**39:5** "How I shall recognize him, lord, I do not know," I said. "Listen," he said. "When a fit of anger or bitterness comes upon you, know that he is in you. And likewise the craving for many transactions, the extravagance of rich foods and excessive drinking, diverse and needless pleasures, desire for women, avarice, overweening pride and boastfulness, and all things like and akin to these — when these things arise in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is in you."

**39:6** "Since then you know his works, withdraw from him and place no trust in him at all, for his works are evil and harmful to the servants of God. You have before you, then, the works of both angels. Understand them, and trust the angel of righteousness."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and precision.*
